title: Nouns, Verbs and Adjectives (KS1)
subject: English
strapline: The three word types that build every sentence.
facts: A noun is a naming word — a person, place, animal or thing: dog, school, Sam, table.
A proper noun is the special name of one particular person or place and starts with a capital letter: London, Monday, Priya.
A verb is a doing or being word — it tells you the action: run, jump, is, sing, think.
An adjective is a describing word — it tells you more about a noun: red, tall, happy, spiky.
You can put an adjective in front of a noun: "the spiky hedgehog", "a tall tree".
A test for a verb: can you say "I can ___" or "she is ___ing"? If yes, it is usually a verb.
A sentence usually needs at least a noun and a verb: "Dogs bark."

quick_quiz.q: In "The happy dog ran fast", which word is the adjective?
Name the verb in "She sings a song".
Is "London" a common noun or a proper noun?

teacher_tips: Sort real objects or picture cards into noun/verb/adjective piles to make it physical.
Play "adjective + noun" games: how many words can describe this apple?
Avoid over-labelling early — spotting them in the child's own writing matters most.
